Question
========

Gegeben sei der DAG `g` (s. u.). Welche minimale Variablenmenge muss kontrolliert werden, um den kausalen Effekt von `x3` (UV) auf `x5` (AV) zu identifizieren?


*Hinweise*: 

- Mengen sind mittels geschweifter Klammern gekennzeichnet, z.B. `{x8, x9}` meint die Menge mit den Elementen `x8` und `x9`.
- Die leere Menge `{ }` bedeutet, dass keine Variable kontrolliert werden muss, um den kausalen Effekt zu identifizieren.


```{r create-dag}
dag_size <- 6
p <- 0.5

g <- randomDAG(N = dag_size, p)


adj <- adjustmentSets(g, 
               exposure = "x3",
               outcome = "x5")  # this is the CORRECT answer

# adj

# it is impossible to get a minimal adjustment set, where one set is empty and
# the second is non-empty

```


```{r check1, eval = FALSE}
library(mosaic)

x <- list()

for (i in 1:1000){
   tmp <- randomDAG(N = dag_size, p)
   x[[i]] <- adjustmentSets(g, 
               exposure = "x3",
               outcome = "x5")
}

```



```{r}
# str(adj)
# length(adj)
# adj[[1]]
# adj <- c("x1, x2")


variables <- paste0("x", 1:dag_size)

variables <- c(variables, " ")

#variables <- paste0("{ ", variables, " }")

sol <- character()

# if there's only one solution set:
if (length(adj) == 1){
  # get all solutions as elements in a string vector:
  z_set <- str_extract_all(adj, pattern = boundary("word")) %>% unlist()
  
  # if there's no solution, define solution as an empty string:
  if (z_set == "list") z_set <- " "
  
  # if (z_set == "{}") z_set <- "???"
  
  # the rest of the variables are therefore incorrect solutions:
  incorrect_z_set <- variables %>% sample() %>% setdiff(z_set)
  
  # enframe those variables with curly braces:
  incorrect_z_set <- paste0("{ ", incorrect_z_set, " }")
  
  # add some variable combiation to the list of incorrect solutions:
  incorrect_z_comb <- paste0("{ ", variables[1], ", ", variables[2], " }")
  incorrect_z <- c(incorrect_z_set, incorrect_z_comb)
  
  sol[1] <- paste0("{ ", z_set[1], " }")  # correct solution
  sol[2:5] <- sample(incorrect_z, 4)  # incorrect solution
}


# if there's more than one solution set, we just pick one randomly as the correct answer:
if (length(adj) > 1){
  z_set <- str_extract_all(adj, pattern = boundary("word")) %>% unlist()
  z_set <- sample(z_set)  # shuffle it
  #if (z_set == "list") z_set <- "{}"
  incorrect_z_set <- variables %>% setdiff(z_set)
  incorrect_z_set <- paste0("{ ", incorrect_z_set, " }")
  incorrect_z_comb <- paste0("{ ", variables[1], ", ", variables[2], " }")  
  incorrect_z <- c(incorrect_z_set, incorrect_z_comb)
  sol[1] <- paste0("{ ", z_set[1], " }")  # correct solution
  sol[2:5] <- sample(incorrect_z, 4) # incorrect solution
}


sol_df <-
  tibble(
    sol = sol,
    is_correct = c(TRUE, F, F, F, F)
  ) %>% 
  sample_n(size = nrow(.))  # shuffle it


# knitr::kable(sol_df)
```





```{r questionlist, results="asis"}
answerlist(sol_df$sol, 
           markup = "markdown")
```




Solution
========

Folgende Variablenmenge muss kontrolliert werden, um den kausalen Effekt von `x3` auf `x5` zu identifizieren: ``r sol_df$sol[sol_df$is_correct == TRUE]``.


*Erläuterung*:

```{r}
is_dseparated <- dseparated(g, X = "x3", Y = "x5")
is_dconnected <- dconnected(g, X = "x3", Y = "x5")
```


`x3` (UV) und `x5` (AV) sind `r ifelse(is_dconnected==FALSE, "nicht", "")` (durch mindestens einen offenen Pfad) verbunden ("d-connected").


Folgende Unabhängigkeitsbeziehungen (`_||_`) werden durch den DAG definiert:
```{r}
impliedConditionalIndependencies(g)
```

`x3` und `x5` werden durch folgende Pfade verbunden:

```{r}

g_paths <- paths(g,
      from = "x3",
      to = "x5")

g_paths
```


Offenen Pfade sind der/die Pfad/e mit der/den Nummer/n: `r which(g_paths$open)`.


Aufgabenname: `_kausal11`





```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
answerlist(ifelse(sol_df$is_correct, "Richtig", "Falsch"), markup = "markdown")
```
